elements.axName: Mario Silva's avatar Follow marios Mario Silva $22M FA @marios Jan 14 Apple could have signed a life-changing deal with Gemini! I think that most investors are already aware of this deal, but most people are still not aware of how this deal can change $AAPL Apple's AI failures in the last years to develop an AI model that fits perfectly with its core values. Most analysts were bashing Apple in the last years because it was not able to go at the same pace as the AI developments built by the other M7. There was a big reason why the AI requirements for Apple were way more challenging than those of the other big techs. The reason is that Cook did not want to train the data in external data centers, where the user's data stop being private, to be a tool that is used for those big techs. As such, Cook wanted each Apple device to train the data for AI "on-device" without the need of external data centers. If a user requires more AI capacity, Apple offers the Private Cloud Computing (PCC), where the user's data will be deleted as soon as it is used. Maybe you are thinking, "Why does Apple care about the privacy and security of the user's data?" Well, to understand it, we need to review which were the core principles developed by Tim Cook since he took over as CEO in 2011. Indeed, since Tim Cook took over as CEO of Apple in 2011, he has set six pillars over which his leadership will thrive in the next few years. I took this information from the book Tim Cook: The Genius Who Took Apple to the Next Level, written by Leander Kahney: Accessibility: Apple considers accessibility a fundamental human right, and technology should be accessible to everybody in the world. Education: Apple considers education a fundamental human right, and high-quality education should be available for everybody in the world. Inclusion and Diversity: Apple considers that diverse teams are what make innovation possible. Environment: Apple boosts environmental responsibility in the design and manufacturing of its products. Privacy and Security: Apple considers privacy a fundamental human right. Every Apple product is designed from scratch to protect the privacy and security of each user. Responsibility of suppliers: Apple educates and empowers its different suppliers within its supply chain while helping in the conservation of the most precious environmental resources. These foundations have been the pillars over which Apple has delivered over 1800% of stock appreciation since Cook started as CEO in 2011. Now, maybe you still have many doubts about why privacy and security are very important for users, particularly in AI. Nobody is paying attention now to this important matter, but the other big techs are gaining a lot of power using their users' data freely, and there are no boundaries to how they are using them. Sooner or later, this will be an issue that these big techs will need to tackle if the government and regulators decide to act to protect users. So, Apple does not want to be caught off guard, and it's the first one working hard since the very beginning to develop an AI that fits with this core pillar: the privacy and security of the user's data. It was in this particular context, when Apple had already exhausted its own possibilities to develop this kind of AI model for itself, that a new and complex agreement was signed with Alphabet to provide a suitable AI development that fulfills Apple's requirements. Some interesting points about the agreement in which Apple will have to pay USD 1 billion to Google: 1. It's a "White Label" Deal (Apple Runs the Brain) Contrary to how most people use AI (sending data to a company like OpenAI or Google), Apple isn't "sending" you to Google. The "Weight" Transfer: Apple has essentially licensed the "model weights" (the brain) of Gemini. The Private Cloud: Instead of running Gemini in Google’s data centers, Apple is running a custom, "sanitized" version of Gemini on its own Private Cloud Compute (PCC). This uses Apple’s own custom silicon (M-series chips) that are physically designed to be "stateless"—meaning they process your request and then "forget" everything instantly. 2.
